reason: Negates 'stoloniferous', which the previous review mapped to stolon present (C208), so this word means stolon absent.

'White-powdered' means covered with a flour-like powder, the same reading as farinose and powdery (C223, C343). 'The powdered rhizomes' is about preparing a drug, not a quality, and should be dropped from the rule.
'Prop' only occurs in 'prop roots', which is a part. PO has prop root.
'Anther refuse at apex' and 'cotyledons refuse' are a misreading of 'retuse' (rounded end with a notch in the centre). The word 'refuse' has no botanical meaning of its own.

label: root-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a root: slender, cylindrical and usually branched. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002457 leaf-like and FLOPO:0991200 bract-like, worded as they are.
reason: Used for submerged leaves (Salvinia), rhizomes and buttresses. It fits the existing '-like' shape family, but there are only 3 statements, so this is a weak case.
A utricle is a fruit type. PO has it with the EXACT synonym utricle. Statements that attach it to a seed or perianth are describing the fruit.
The meaning is unclear: for moss spores it usually means unequal size, for stamens unequal shape. Neither FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic (exactly two forms) nor FLOPO:0991101 unequal fits safely.
This is a width-to-length ratio of 1 for the same part, not a quality term.
'Broadly' is only a degree word on 'bordered' (a margin of different cells, as in mosses), and 'bordered' has no term or rule yet. Review the base word, not this phrase.
This joins two values on one margin: ciliated (PATO_0001408) and papillose. It should be split into two qualities, not given a term of its own.

'Calyx limb degraded' and 'central strand degraded' mean reduced to a remnant, the same reading as obsolete and rudimentary (C234, C142). PATO 'degenerate' means a disease process, so it does not fit.
'Leaves densely placed' means set close together on the axis, which is crowded. The whole-plant example is a cut-off 'densely tufted' that is already covered by caespitose.
Like 'covered' (C240), it needs to say what covers the part (soil, scales). The covering is the quality, and soil is not a trait at all.
It describes how separate stems or leaves are mixed together in a clump. That is vague and not a quality of a single part.
It only says the members vary in shape, with no defined set of forms. PATO pleomorphic (one cell changing shape over its life cycle) does not fit.
'Narrowly' is a degree word that measurements already cover. The shape is cylindrical.
This is a shape between two values: rhomboid (PATO_0001938) with rounded angles. It is like 'oblong-ovate' and needs no term of its own.
Leaves and fruits 'shrinking' usually means on drying, which is the state of the specimen, not a living trait. Where it is stated, the quality would be PATO_0002460 shriveled.
This is a general part name that needs its organ: costa teeth, peristome tooth (PO_0030043), leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518). It is handled like 'scale' and 'segment'.
Three cell layers thick is a count. Unistratose and bistratose should be handled the same way, as a count of cell layers rather than one term per number.
It means different things here: brightly coloured cells (mosses) versus fresh, not-withering bracts. No single safe mapping exists.
Glossaries define obovate as broadest above the middle, and floras use this phrase for the same outline in leaves and fruits.
'Costa ending in or below the apex' links the costa to another part (apex, margin). Where it means 'reaching the apex', FLOPO:0991163 percurrent applies.
Naviculiform means boat-shaped, the same reading as boat-shaped and cymbiform (C213, C215).
This is a label left over from the extraction step, not a word in the floras. The examples are presence statements that other rules already handle.
It describes how far old cataphylls have broken down into fibres. That is vague, and persistence is already covered by the existing persistent and marcescent terms.
A siliqua is a fruit type. PO lists siliqua as a synonym of silique fruit.
Same reading as 'widened' (C182). 'Slightly' is a degree word.
Same meaning as awnless (C347) and muticous (C348).
Untoothed means not toothed. It negates PATO dentated (synonym toothed), built the same way as 'unlobed' (C239).
